name: Babbel
tagline: Build a personal lesson and review tool from user-supplied material

pricing.notes: Typical one-month subscription price; regional offers vary.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Babbel, build a personal lesson and review tool from user-supplied material. The hard boundary is professionally authored curriculum, speech practice, courses, apps, and pedagogy, plus content, pedagogy, and network.
coreLoopDIY: Turn user-supplied language material into lessons and a study plan, schedule retrieval practice, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
requirements: optional speech or language-model API key
whatYouLose: professionally authored curriculum, speech practice, courses, apps, and pedagogy
ongoingBurden: curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Babbel because the learning loop is buildable, while trusted curriculum, instructors, feedback, credentials, and community are not. The recurring cost buys curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Moodle
priorArt.desc: Long-running open-source learning platform with courses, assessments, and progress tracking.

alternatives.name: Anki
alternatives.desc: User-authored language lessons become serious spaced-repetition cards with audio, images and progress history.

facts.install: Use the Windows installer, macOS DMG or official Linux launcher
facts.dataFormat: Local profile files including collection.anki2, collection.media and backups; exports use .apkg/.colpkg, with optional AnkiWeb sync
facts.gapVsPaid: Anki supplies no expert-authored curriculum, grammar path, dialogue practice or automatic pronunciation coaching; the learner must build or source the material.

alternatives.name: AnkiDroid
alternatives.desc: The same user-built lesson deck on Android, minus the owl, streak theatre and subscription.

facts.install: Install from Google Play or F-Droid, or sideload the official APK
facts.dataFormat: An Anki collection and media on the Android device, with .apkg import/export and optional AnkiWeb sync
facts.gapVsPaid: AnkiDroid supplies no expert-authored curriculum, grammar path or pronunciation coaching; the learner must build or source the material.

alternatives.name: Moodle
alternatives.desc: A full course system for lessons, quizzes and review; sensible for a class, excessive for ordering one coffee.

facts.install: Upload the PHP release to a web server, create a database and moodledata directory, then complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Courses, users, grades and settings in SQL; uploaded files in the separate moodledata directory
facts.gapVsPaid: Moodle supplies no expert-made language curriculum, pronunciation engine or daily conversational flow, and running an LMS is excessive for one learner.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP and database requirements, protected writable storage, cron, SMTP, backups and upgrades are all the operator's responsibility

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Babbel subscription plan and a personal study companion DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Babbel in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and a service worker for offline use; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: turn user-supplied language material into lessons and a study plan, schedule retrieval practice, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Import Markdown, text, or user-authored notes and split them into editable learning units.
Create flashcards and short quizzes only after showing the generated items for approval.
Implement a transparent spaced-repetition schedule with due, again, hard, good, and easy actions.
Add goals, study sessions, streak-free progress charts, notes, and weak-topic review.
For language practice, record the learner and compare timing or pronunciation without presenting medical claims.
Support offline use, full export, reset, backup, and deletion of all learning data.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out licensed premium courses.
Deliberately leave out accredited certificates and grading.
Deliberately leave out live tutors, large classrooms, and a learner marketplace.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
